subject.title: fix(codex): coalesce in-flight dynamic tool calls

question: Should OpenClaw treat same-turn Codex dynamic-tool requests with different `callId` values but identical payloads as duplicate deliveries that may share one external execution?
rationale: The upstream protocol distinguishes these requests by call identity, while the proposed semantic equivalence rule is intentionally narrower and has not been established as a Codex contract.

options.title: Require a protocol-backed retry identity
options.body: Merge only after the implementation keys coalescing to an upstream-confirmed duplicate/retry identity and preserves call-scoped observability.

options.title: Adopt payload equivalence as OpenClaw policy
options.body: Accept that identical in-flight payloads are one logical operation and document the deliberate loss of distinct-call execution semantics.

options.title: Keep distinct calls independent
options.body: Do not merge this coalescer and address duplicate delivery only at a layer that can prove retry identity.

recommendation.title: Require a protocol-backed retry identity
recommendation.body: Merge only after the implementation keys coalescing to an upstream-confirmed duplicate/retry identity and preserves call-scoped observability.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available adjacent-routing candidate for the Codex app-server lifecycle and terminal-invariant decision.
